## Summary

Implemented in `hexadecimal.go` (the only file changed; `hexadecimal_test.go` untouched, no new files):

- **`ParseHex(string) (int64, error)`** — converts hex to decimal from first principles with no library use:
  - Empty string or any non-hex character (`a-f`, `A-F`, `0-9`) → error containing `"syntax"` (all characters are validated first, so a string with bad digits is always a syntax error, even if it would also overflow).
  - Overflow of `int64` → error containing `"range"`, checked each step via `value > (maxInt64-d)/16` before the multiply.
- **`HandleErrors([]string) []string`** — calls `ParseHex` on each input and maps the result to `"none"`, `"syntax"`, or `"range"`.

Verified against all 10 test cases, including the tricky ones: `"8000000000000000"` (equals 2⁶³, overflows) and `"9223372036854775809"` (all valid hex digits, but ~19 hex digits far exceeds int64) both correctly report `"range"`.
